content: 1. The recommended dose of Tramadol should never be exceeded under any circumstances. 2. Tramadol should not be co-administered with other products containing Tramadol or acetaminophen. 3. The safety and effectiveness of Tramadol have not been established in the pediatric population. 4. In elderly patients, dose selection should be approached with caution. This is due to the higher likelihood of reduced hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as the presence of concurrent diseases and the use of multiple medications. 5. The administration of Tramadol in patients with acute abdominal conditions may complicate the clinical evaluation of their condition. 6. Tramadol has not been studied in patients with impaired renal function. Clinical experience suggests that renal impairment leads to a reduced rate and extent of excretion of Tramadol and its active metabolite, M1. For patients with creatinine clearance levels below 30 mL/min, it is recommended to increase the dosing interval, ensuring that no more than two tablets are administered every 12 hours. 7. Tramadol has not been studied in patients with impaired hepatic function. Its use in patients with hepatic impairment is not recommended.
